newsitem.title: USA: Small dealers eye class action against NASD - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Small dealers eye class action against NASD - lawyer.

text.p: Attorneys for former NASD examiner Theresa Carr said they may file a separate class action lawsuit against the association on behalf of a number of small brokerage firms.

Jacob Zamansky, a partner with Singer Zamansky in New York City, said the firms would claim the National Association of Securities Dealer's district 10 office in New York City targets smaller brokerage firms for enforcement action over larger, higher profile firms.

"Smaller firms are treated one way by NASD and larger firms are treated another," the lawsuit would charge, Zamansky said in a telephone interview. "There is a bias at NASD toward bigger firms," he added.
"That is largely because of the composition of NASD's board of governors," said Zamansky, who would not release the names of the firms that want to bring a lawsuit.
Zamansky's firm filed a $20 million damages suit in New York Supreme Court September 4 against NASD and one of its top officials on behalf of former NASD district 10 investigator Theresa Carr.
Carr charged the association forced her to resign because of her aggressive probe of "pay-to-play" by major municipal bond dealers.
NASD says Carr's charges are "meritless" and vows to fight them in court.
NASD, which hired Gibson Dunn & Crutcher attorney Joseph Warin to represent it, is set formally to respond to Carr's charges Nov. 5.
Zamansky said his firm also has decided to bring yet another lawsuit within two weeks on behalf of a second NASD examiner who charges NASD interfered with probes of major securities firms.

Zamansky said the second lawsuit will not involve municipal bond business. Reuters reported Sept. 11 that Zamansky's firm was reviewing the second lawsuit but had not decided whether to take the case.
"The examiner wanted NASD to pursue customer complaints that they were deceived by a major brokerage firm," Zamansky said. The complaints involved "very aggregious circumstances," he said.
